subtopics.title: Insolation and the Earth's Heat Budget

questions.question: Following one hundred units of insolation, the approximate fate of the energy is:
options: 30 reflected to space, 20 absorbed by the atmosphere, 50 absorbed at the surface
50 reflected, 30 absorbed by the atmosphere, 20 reaching the surface
100 absorbed by the atmosphere
70 reflected, 30 reaching the surface

questions.question: A surface with HIGH albedo is one that:
options: Absorbs nearly all radiation, like dark ocean water
Reflects a large share of the insolation striking it — snowfields, sea ice and pale pans
Emits no long-wave radiation
Conducts heat rapidly downward

questions.question: The atmosphere catches TERRESTRIAL radiation but lets most SOLAR radiation pass because:
options: Terrestrial radiation travels more slowly
Solar radiation only arrives at night
The atmosphere is a poor absorber of the long waves and a good absorber of the short
The earth, being far cooler than the sun, emits LONG-WAVE energy — and the atmosphere absorbs long waves well while transmitting short waves

questions.question: The heat budget balances for the planet as a whole, yet global circulation still exists, because:
options: The sun's output changes every year
The atmosphere leaks energy into space at the equator only
Latitudes within about 40 degrees of the equator run a permanent energy SURPLUS and higher latitudes a permanent DEFICIT, and winds and currents must carry the difference poleward
Volcanoes reheat the poles

subtopics.title: How Heat Moves — Radiation, Conduction, Convection, Advection

questions.question: The only heat-transfer process able to cross the vacuum between sun and earth is:
options: Radiation — energy travelling as electromagnetic waves, needing no medium
Conduction
Convection
Advection

questions.question: Conduction affects only the thin skin of air touching the ground because:
options: The ground blocks the process
Air is a POOR conductor, so molecule-to-molecule transfer cannot reach far beyond the contact layer
Conduction requires moisture
The wind removes conducted heat

questions.question: A blazing Free State morning often ends in an afternoon thunderstorm because:
options: The berg wind arrives at noon
Ocean currents shift inland in summer
Conduction reaches cloud height on hot days
Surface-warmed air expands, rises and is replaced by sinking cooler air — a CONVECTION current that lifts heat and moisture to cloud-building height

questions.question: The winter berg wind that pushes the KwaZulu-Natal south coast into the thirties is an example of:
options: Conduction from warm rock
Counter-radiation
ADVECTION — hot, dry interior air transferred horizontally off the plateau toward the sea
Convection over the ocean

subtopics.title: The Greenhouse Effect and Enhanced Warming

questions.question: Placed in strict order, the greenhouse mechanism runs:
options: Short-wave passes through the atmosphere, the surface absorbs it and warms, the surface re-emits long-wave, greenhouse gases absorb it, and counter-radiation returns part of it downward
Long-wave arrives from the sun, the atmosphere reflects it, the surface cools, gases trap the cold
Greenhouse gases absorb short-wave, the surface reflects long-wave, clouds trap both
The surface emits short-wave, the sun absorbs it, the atmosphere warms

questions.question: Without the NATURAL greenhouse effect, the global average surface temperature would be roughly:
options: −18 °C instead of about 15 °C — thirty-three degrees of habitability lost

questions.question: Which list contains only human sources of the ENHANCED greenhouse effect?
options: Volcanoes, ocean spray, forest growth
Sunspots, orbital wobble, tides
Fossil-fuel burning, deforestation, cattle and flooded paddies, landfill decay, cement kilns
Ozone formation, sea-ice growth, evaporation

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the lesson's consequences of climate change for Africa?
options: Malaria mosquitoes advancing into once-cool highland areas
Deeper droughts across the south and west
Falling maize yields threatening food security
The Benguela Current reversing to flow southward

subtopics.title: The Five Factors That Set Temperature

questions.question: High latitudes are colder than the equator because slanting rays:
options: Smear the same beam across a wider area AND thread a longer, more absorbing path through the atmosphere
Carry less energy when they leave the sun
Arrive only in summer
Are reflected by the ozone layer

questions.question: Bloemfontein lies near 1 400 m, at almost Durban's latitude. Using 6,5 °C per 1 000 m, altitude alone makes Bloemfontein about:
options: 2 °C cooler
9 °C cooler
20 °C cooler
No different

questions.question: Distance from the sea chiefly controls a place's:
options: Daily wind direction
Cloud type
ANNUAL TEMPERATURE RANGE — coastal Gqeberha stays cushioned while inland De Aar swings from baking to frost
Altitude

questions.question: The correct pairing of South Africa's flanking currents is:
options: Cold Agulhas east, warm Benguela west
Both currents warm, flowing north
Warm Benguela east, cold Agulhas west
Warm AGULHAS south along the east coast bringing East London mild humid air; cold BENGUELA north along the west coast bringing Lambert's Bay fog and dryness

questions.question: In the delivery story, the thirty buckets 'tipped back at the gate' stand for:
options: Albedo — insolation reflected off cloud tops, dust and bright surfaces before doing any work
Energy absorbed by ozone
The heat stored in the oceans
Counter-radiation

questions.question: The ground 'pours its fifty buckets back in a different form', meaning:
options: It reflects the sunshine unchanged
Energy that arrived as short-wave sunshine leaves the cool earth as LONG-WAVE heat — which the atmosphere catches on the way out
It converts sunlight into wind directly
It stores the energy underground forever

questions.question: 'Every gale is a delivery truck balancing the planet's accounts' because:
options: Winds blow only where energy is equal
Storms destroy surplus energy
The tropics permanently receive more energy than they lose and the poles the reverse, so winds and currents cart the surplus poleward
The sun powers the wind at the poles first

questions.question: Scalding sand under pleasant air proves that:
options: Sunshine passes through air and heats SURFACES — the atmosphere is heated from below, by the ground
Air absorbs most of the sun's energy directly
Sand generates its own heat
The sea cools the air first

questions.question: On the beach, the burn on your bare soles is the process of:
options: Radiation
Conduction — heat crossing by direct touch, exactly how the ground heats the first layer of air
Convection
Advection

questions.question: The shimmer wobbling above hot sand is small-scale:
options: Advection
Albedo
Convection — warmed air rising in columns while cooler air slides in beneath, the same motion that builds afternoon thunderclouds inland
Counter-radiation

questions.question: The three o'clock sea breeze is advection because it:
options: Rises vertically off the water
Radiates across empty space
Passes heat by direct contact
Moves cool marine air HORIZONTALLY onto the land

subtopics.title: Why Musina Swelters and Molteno Freezes

questions.question: The hosepipe comparison — straight down soaks a small circle, tilted scatters thin — explains:
options: LATITUDE: Musina's near-vertical sun is concentrated, Molteno's slanted sun is spread and weakened
Ocean currents
Cloud cover
Aspect

questions.question: Molteno starts every winter night 'with a head start toward frost' because:
options: It lies furthest from the equator of any town
It sits above 1 700 m, and altitude costs about 6,5 °C per 1 000 m of climb away from the ground that heats the air
The Benguela Current flows past it
It has the country's highest rainfall

questions.question: De Aar leaps to the high thirties in January yet freezes on July nights because:
options: It has high albedo
Its aspect faces south
It lies far from any ocean, so no slow-changing water steadies its temperatures — a huge annual range
The Agulhas Current warms it in summer only

questions.question: Molteno's coldest nights need CLEAR skies because:
options: Clouds produce frost directly
Clear air conducts heat upward faster
Starlight warms cloudy nights
Cloud acts as a two-way shield — without it, every scrap of daytime heat escapes to space after dark and the minimum plunges
